001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
004import java.util.ArrayList;
005import java.util.List;
006import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
007import java.util.concurrent.atomic.LongAdder;
008
009/**
010 * Metrics are cheap, numeric counters about the logging system itself - for example how
011 * many events an appender has dropped, or how often a reused encoder buffer had to shrink
012 * itself back down. Unlike {@link LogAlerts}, which records discrete events (each with a
013 * message/throwable, kept in a bounded ring buffer), metrics are just running totals: no
014 * per-call allocation, no ring buffer entry, no listener dispatch.
015 * <p>
016 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#metrics()}. Components that are
017 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
018 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
019 * capturing {@code config.metrics()} over reaching for global state.
020 * <p>
021 * Deliberately a separate type from {@link LogAlerts} rather than more methods on it -
022 * the two are meant to be independently replaceable (e.g. a future Micrometer-backed
023 * {@code LogMetrics} without needing to also replace how alerts are recorded).
024 *
025 * @see LogConfig#metrics()
026 */
027public sealed interface LogMetrics permits DefaultLogMetrics {
028
029        /**
030         * Counter name for the global count of log events dropped without ever being written
031         * anywhere - for example an appender dropping events on reentry. Incremented whenever
032         * a drop happens regardless of whether that particular drop is also logged/alerted,
033         * since counting and alerting/logging are separate concerns.
034         */
035        static final String EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC = "events.dropped";
036
037        /**
038         * Counter name for the global count of times a reused encoder buffer had its backing
039         * storage shrunk back down after growing past its configured max size (see
040         * {@link LogEncoder.Buffer#isOversized()}). An occasional trim is normal and expected
041         * once in a while, but resizing <em>often</em> is a sign the configured max size (or
042         * the initial size) doesn't match the actual event sizes being logged - worth
043         * watching, not erroring on, hence {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} rather than
044         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}.
045         */
046        static final String BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC = "buffer.trimmed";
047
048        /**
049         * Counter name for the global count of log events an appender failed to write - the
050         * encoder or output threw while appending, so the event was caught, alerted (see
051         * {@link LogAlerts#error(Class, String, Throwable)}), and lost rather than retried.
052         * Kept separate from {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}: a drop is a deliberate skip (the
053         * appender chose not to write), while this is an unexpected failure partway through
054         * actually trying to - different root causes worth distinguishing when triaging.
055         */
056        static final String EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC = "events.failed";
057
058        /**
059         * Counter name for the running count of distinct logger names registered via
060         * {@link LogConfig.LoggerRegistry#registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}. Not itself
061         * a problem, hence {@link #infoCounter(String, long)} rather than
062         * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, but worth watching: a count that keeps climbing
063         * without bound is a sign something is using per-request/per-entity data (e.g. a
064         * request id) as a logger name instead of a fixed, bounded set of names.
065         */
066        static final String LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC = "logger.names";
067
068        /**
069         * Increments a counter for something worth tracking as "this happens and it matters".
070         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC} or a logger name.
071         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
072         */
073        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment);
074
075        /**
076         * Like {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} but for something worth tracking yet less
077         * significant than an error - a trend worth watching rather than something that, by
078         * itself, indicates a problem. Kept as a separate counter namespace from
079         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}: the same {@code name} passed to both is two
080         * distinct counters, not one shared one.
081         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
082         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
083         */
084        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment);
085
086        /**
087         * Like {@link #errorCounter(String, long)} but for a plain running total, not
088         * inherently a problem or even a trend worth watching. Kept as a separate counter
089         * namespace from
090         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}/{@link #warnCounter(String, long)}: the same
091         * {@code name} passed to more than one of these is a distinct counter per method, not
092         * one shared one.
093         * @param name counter name, e.g. {@link #LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC}.
094         * @param increment amount to add, usually {@code 1}.
095         */
096        public void infoCounter(String name, long increment);
097
098        /**
099         * A snapshot of every counter recorded via {@link #errorCounter(String, long)},
100         * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, and {@link #infoCounter(String, long)}.
101         * Counters are monotonically increasing for the life of the process, like a
102         * Prometheus/Micrometer counter - there is no reset method; a downstream metrics
103         * system computes rate of change rather than relying on the counter itself being
104         * reset.
105         * @return immutable snapshot.
106         */
107        public List<Counter> counters();
108
109        /**
110         * A single named counter's current value, as returned by {@link #counters()}.
111         *
112         * @param name counter name, as passed to a counter method like
113         * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}.
114         * @param level how much this counter matters - not a log level routing decision, just
115         * a signal of significance, mirroring the counter method it came from (e.g.
116         * {@link Level#ERROR} for {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#WARNING}
117         * for {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#INFO} for
118         * {@link #infoCounter(String, long)}).
119         * @param count current value.
120         */
121        record Counter(String name, Level level, long count) {
122        }
123
124        /**
125         * The fixed, well known set of counters RainbowGum itself records - as opposed to the
126         * open ended, per logger name counters {@link LogAlerts#error(LogEvent)} also drives
127         * into {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}. Enumerable on purpose: consumers that
128         * want to bind every well known counter to something else (a Micrometer
129         * {@code FunctionCounter} per constant, for example) can loop over {@link #values()}
130         * instead of hand listing each {@code String}/{@link Level} pair themselves.
131         */
132        enum StandardMetric {
133
134                /**
135                 * See {@link #EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC}.
136                 */
137                EVENTS_DROPPED(EVENTS_DROPPED_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
138                /**
139                 * See {@link #BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
140                 */
141                BUFFER_TRIMMED(BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, Level.WARNING),
142                /**
143                 * See {@link #EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC}.
144                 */
145                EVENTS_FAILED(EVENTS_FAILED_METRIC, Level.ERROR),
146                /**
147                 * See {@link #LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC}.
148                 */
149                LOGGER_NAMES(LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC, Level.INFO);
150
151                private final String metricName;
152
153                private final Level level;
154
155                StandardMetric(String metricName, Level level) {
156                        this.metricName = metricName;
157                        this.level = level;
158                }
159
160                /**
161                 * The counter name, as passed to {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}/
162                 * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)} and matched against {@link Counter#name()}.
163                 * @return counter name.
164                 */
165                public String metricName() {
166                        return metricName;
167                }
168
169                /**
170                 * Which counter method this metric is recorded through - {@link Level#ERROR} for
171                 * {@link #errorCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#WARNING} for
172                 * {@link #warnCounter(String, long)}, {@link Level#INFO} for
173                 * {@link #infoCounter(String, long)} - and so also which {@link Counter#level()}
174                 * it shows up under in {@link #counters()}.
175                 * @return level.
176                 */
177                public Level level() {
178                        return level;
179                }
180
181        }
182
183}
184
185final class DefaultLogMetrics implements LogMetrics {
186
187        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> errorCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
188
189        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> warnCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
190
191        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> infoCounters = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
192
193        @Override
194        public void errorCounter(String name, long increment) {
195                errorCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
196        }
197
198        @Override
199        public void warnCounter(String name, long increment) {
200                warnCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
201        }
202
203        @Override
204        public void infoCounter(String name, long increment) {
205                infoCounters.computeIfAbsent(name, k -> new LongAdder()).add(increment);
206        }
207
208        @Override
209        public List<Counter> counters() {
210                List<Counter> list = new ArrayList<>(errorCounters.size() + warnCounters.size() + infoCounters.size());
211                for (var e : errorCounters.entrySet()) {
212                        list.add(new Counter(e.getKey(), Level.ERROR, e.getValue().sum()));
213                }
214                for (var e : warnCounters.entrySet()) {
215                        list.add(new Counter(e.getKey(), Level.WARNING, e.getValue().sum()));
216                }
217                for (var e : infoCounters.entrySet()) {
218                        list.add(new Counter(e.getKey(), Level.INFO, e.getValue().sum()));
219                }
220                return List.copyOf(list);
221        }
222
223}
